evidence.V1: Stepped profile is instantly readable as stairs in silhouette, three-quarter and front.
evidence.V2: Big (4 steps) and small (tread nosing lips) only; no medium tier such as stringers, side cheek blocks or block joints, so the side is one large blank face.
evidence.V3: A plain extruded step profile with equal boxy treads; stiff primitive with no stylised exaggeration (no chunky stringer, uneven blocks or wear).
evidence.V4: Tread nosings have consistent rounded lips that catch light, but riser corners and the side/back vertical edges read hard in the side close-up.
evidence.V5: Side close-up shows diagonal dark smears across the large side face (weighted-normal shading streak from the step corners); minor artifact.
evidence.V6: One stone hue in 3 values (light treads, mid nosing, dark risers/side); consistent in brick and sandstone colourways.
evidence.V7: 148 tris vs module target 800; very economical.
evidence.V8: Correct material and bevel scale, but no accents or block articulation; reads blander than the kit's detailed stone modules.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct (Anchored, CollisionFidelity Default or wedge for walking, CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic); T1 tiling pass.

artifacts: diagonal shading smears on the side face near step corners
top_fixes: Add a stringer/cheek wall on the open side or cut the side into stone blocks so the large flat side gets medium detail and loses the shading smear
Vary tread blocks (split each tread into 2-3 stones, slight height/width variation) for stylised proportion
Chamfer the vertical riser and side edges to match the nosing bevel
